summary: Per-strut suspension contact solver. Iterates the vehicle suspension strut array (this+0x134, stride 316) for a count derived from this+0x130 (all struts) or 1 (single-strut mode when a2 is non-zero). For each strut with a live linked node (+268) and contact feature (+272), queries the spatial grid, extracts the collision normal, builds a contact frame, applies gravity compensation, and runs ray-sphere intersection tests to write penetration depth and contact force at strut offsets +112/+116/+120/+124/+128.

local_names.this: vehicle physics node carrying the strut array
local_names.a2: strut selector; non-zero forces single-strut mode
local_names.v51: byte stride accumulator over the strut array

operations.description: Iteration count = (a2 != 0) ? 1 : this+0x130; the whole loop body only runs while the count is greater than 0
Walk the suspension strut array whose base is this+0x134, stepping 316 bytes per strut; in single-strut mode the selector a2 supplies the strut pointer directly
Reset per-strut contact state: strut+112 and +116 set to 0, strut+120 set to 0, strut+124 set to a negative literal, strut+128 set to 0
Per-strut processing only proceeds when both the linked node at strut+268 and the contact feature pointer at strut+272 are non-zero
SpatialGridQuery on the feature position read at node+148/+152/+156, filling the query struct that drives contact lookup
CollisionNormalFromFeature extracts the collision surface normal into the v33 buffer when the grid query hits
Second SpatialGridQuery on the strut wheel position (strut+148/+152/+156) to locate the strut-side contact feature
Displacement vector between the strut wheel position and the feature position; the frame construction is guarded on its norm being non-zero
Cross products of the normal axis pairs and normalization build the contact frame axes (basis constants 0, 1, 2 encoded in the query struct)
Gravity compensation: dot products of the contact frame axes with the gravity vector (-9.8100004) are folded into the three contact force components
RaySphereQuadraticIntersectionTest run twice with the frame-projected parameters; results become the penetration depths written to strut+112 and strut+116, with sign corrections applied after
Write the gravity-compensated contact force components back to the strut at +120/+124/+128 and the penetration depths to +112/+116
Decrement the remaining count and advance the byte stride by 316 for the next strut, continuing until the count reaches zero
Return the final loop counter value; the function is invoked per strut by SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection (00401910) and PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff (00401C90)
